title: Delights of Paradise and the Prophet's Reminder

paragraphs.text: The people of the Fire will be told to enter and burn in it. Whether they bear it patiently or complain, it makes no difference for them, because they are only being paid back for what they used to do.

The righteous, in contrast, will live in gardens and delight, enjoying what their Lord has given them, and He has protected them from the punishment of Hellfire. They will be invited to eat and drink with satisfaction as a reward for their deeds. They will recline on thrones arranged in rows, and Allah will marry them to fair companions with large, beautiful eyes. Those who believed, and whose children followed them in faith, will have their descendants joined with them, while nothing will be reduced from their own deeds. Every person is held responsible for what he earned. They will receive fruit and meat of whatever they desire. They will pass a cup among themselves that leads to no foolish talk and no sin, and young servants, like protected pearls, will move around them.

The people of Paradise will turn to one another and talk about their past. They will remember that, while living among their families, they were fearful of displeasing Allah. Because of this, Allah showed them His favor and saved them from the scorching Fire. They will add that they used to call upon Him in prayer before, and that He is truly the Beneficent, the Merciful.

The Prophet is told to continue reminding people. By his Lord's favor, he is neither a fortune-teller nor a madman. Some say he is merely a poet and that they are waiting for some misfortune to strike him. He is told to answer that they may wait, and he too will wait along with them. The passage then asks whether their own minds truly lead them to such claims, or whether they are simply a people who go beyond limits.

hardWords.m: a person who claims to know the future
